speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble eating and your tummy looks swollen. Can you tell me if you are vomiting, and if so, does it look like coffee grounds or does it have a foul smell?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: The baby seems to be in significant pain with abdominal tenderness. Has there been any blood in the stool, or has the baby passed gas or had a bowel movement recently? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count and Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work is normal, which is helpful. Since the baby is crying when the abdomen is touched and has distension, have you noticed a palpable mass or a "sausage-shaped" bowel loop, and does he pass stool at all? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work and metabolic panel are normal, which rules out systemic infection or metabolic errors. Did you notice any blood mixed with mucus in his stool, and can you feel a firm, sausage-shaped mass in his abdomen? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: No fever or infection signs, which is good. However, the history of crying with abdominal palpation and the request for an abdominal ultrasound are highly suggestive of a specific surgical condition. Since the ultrasound request was made earlier but results weren't explicitly detailed as "normal" regarding the bowel itself (only blood work was explicitly normal), does the baby have a history of failure to pass meconium in the first 48 hours of life? DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception
